title: Marguerite and the Parish
premise: When a confession letter arrives at coroner Jonah Coldharbour's office postmarked the day after Marguerite Voss's funeral, it claims her drowning was no accident — and that the parish council buried the truth along with her. Jonah, who signed off on the death twelve years ago, must retrace their own alphabetized lies through a hidden ledger kept in the church's memorial plaques, while someone on the council begins silencing anyone who remembers. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Jonah uncovers that the ledger's final entry names them — a price they once accepted to survive. In the end, Jonah chooses truth over self-preservation, testifying as the statute expires, and the parish's power structure collapses with Marguerite finally given her true cause of death.
about_author: Beatrix Thornbury is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing small-town deaths before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted vestry office, where she insists the drafts are better for the smell of old paper.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Jonah Coldharbour, POV. Establishes Jonah's meticulous filing of twelve years of parish deaths and their quiet pride in knowing every grave. A confession letter arrives postmarked the day after Marguerite Voss's funeral, naming Jonah directly. Emotional beat: unease cracking a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: Drowned on a Dry Night
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah rereads their own twelve-year-old coroner's report and finds an inconsistency: rain in the margins, but no rain that night. They visit Marguerite's grave and find fresh lilies — her favorite, though no one living should know. Beat: guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Council of Nine
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The parish council, led by patriarch Aldous Crane, welcomes Jonah warmly at the memorial supper — too warmly. Jonah realizes the letter's author may be among the nine. Beat: paranoia dressed in cassocks and casseroles.

chapters.title: What the Widow Kept
chapters.summary: Widow Edith Marsh's POV. Edith, Marguerite's sister-in-law, reveals Marguerite kept a private ledger of parish tithes — and that she burned nothing. She gives Jonah Marguerite's hymnal, its pages hollowed. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Names in the Woodwork
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah discovers the memorial plaques in the church nave carry initials that don't match any parish register — a code. Cross-referencing with Marguerite's hymnal, the first three entries decode to payments. Beat: the thrill of the hidden made visible.

chapters.title: A Visit from Aldous
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Crane offers Jonah a seat on the council — a gilded silencing. He mentions, casually, the statute of limitations and Jonah's signature on the old report. Beat: the price of survival made explicit, and Jonah's fear that they already paid it once.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Saw
chapters.summary: Tobias Fenwick's POV, now a grown man. Tobias was fourteen the night Marguerite died and saw lanterns at the reservoir. He has stayed silent for twelve years, but the funeral cracked something open. Beat: the cost of childhood silence.

chapters.title: Ledger, Entry Four
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The fourth decoded entry names a payment dated the week before Marguerite's death — to a doctor who certified it. Jonah learns the doctor retired to the coast. Beat: the conspiracy widening beyond the parish.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah traces the confession letter's postmark to the parish's own mail room and realizes the author wanted the letter to arrive — publicly, traceably. Someone inside is forcing the truth open. Beat: hope entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Coast Road
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah drives to find the retired doctor and finds him freshly dead — an 'accident' that echoes Marguerite's. In his study, a copy of the ledger with one page torn out. Beat: dread; the silencing has begun in earnest.

chapters.title: Edith's Warning
chapters.summary: Edith, POV. Edith is followed home and her cottage searched. She warns Jonah that Crane's family has run the parish for a century and that Marguerite found out why: the ledger records tithes extracted from the poor to buy the council's land cheaply. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Ago
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV, interwoven flashback. The night of Marguerite's death: young Jonah, new to the job, is handed the report to sign by the old coroner — and by Crane. They signed to keep their position, to survive. Beat: shame fully confessed to the reader.

chapters.title: Entry Nine
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The ninth ledger entry is Jonah's own initials — the payment for their silence, recorded by Marguerite herself. She knew, and kept the record anyway. Beat: devastation; the ledger was always meant for Jonah to find.

chapters.title: Tobias Breaks
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. Crane's men threaten Tobias's mother. Instead of retreating, Tobias goes to the parish newspaper with his account. Beat: courage against duty's old blackmail; the town begins to murmur.

chapters.title: The Statute
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah consults a lawyer: the statute expires in nine days, after which prosecution for the cover-up becomes impossible. The council only needs to wait them out. Beat: the clock made flesh; Jonah's resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Hollowed Hymnal
chapters.summary: Edith, POV. Edith decodes the final plaques with Jonah: the torn page's contents are recoverable from the stone itself — the last entry records Crane's own signature on Marguerite's death order. Beat: the weapon assembled.

chapters.title: The Vestry Fire
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The church vestry burns overnight, destroying parish records. Jonah, anticipating it, had photographed the plaques. But the fire is a message: they know Jonah has copies. Beat: terror braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Voice
chapters.summary: Edith, POV. Among Marguerite's effects, a sealed letter to Jonah, written before her death: 'You were young and afraid. I recorded you anyway, because the dead need the whole truth, even the ugly parts.' Beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: Nine Days, One Night
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The council moves to have Jonah removed as coroner on fabricated grounds. Jonah goes to the reservoir at night, where Tobias identifies the exact spot, and finds the physical ledger page Marguerite hid in a drainage grate. Beat: the climax's threshold.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. At an emergency town meeting, before the statute expires, Jonah reads the ledger aloud — including their own entry — and submits the amended death certificate: homicide. Crane's allies defect one by one as the room turns. Beat: catharsis through self-indictment.

chapters.title: What the Stone Remembers
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. Crane is arrested; the council dissolves; the land titles are voided. The plaques are recut with honest names, Marguerite's among them, her true dates at last. Beat: a town learning to breathe.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah files the corrected report — the first entry in a new ledger, kept openly in the parish office. They visit Marguerite's grave with lilies, no longer ashamed to know what she loved. Beat: survival redefined as truth-telling; quiet, earned peace.
